resources.string: Every file is scanned before it opens
This app has no internet permission. Your files never leave your phone.

• Word: DOCX, DOCM, DOC, RTF, ODT
• Excel: XLSX, XLSM, XLS, CSV, ODS
• PowerPoint: PPTX, PPTM, PPSX, PPT, ODP
• PDF, EPUB books, HTML pages
• Images: JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, HEIC, SVG, BMP
• Video & audio: MP4, MKV, WEBM, MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC
• ZIP archives (open the files inside)
• Anything else: shown as text or hex

• No internet permission: no file can send your data anywhere.
• Macros, scripts and JavaScript never run, not even in PDFs.
• The scanner detects malicious macros, programs disguised as documents, double extensions, remote templates, Follina, Equation Editor exploits, DDE, PDF JavaScript and auto-actions, zip bombs and dangerous files inside archives.
• Files are opened as a private copy that is deleted when you close it.

To browse every folder (Downloads, WhatsApp…) Android requires the \"All files access\" permission. This app has no internet access, so nothing can leave your phone. Enable it for SafeOpen, then come back.

SafeOpen opens documents, spreadsheets, presentations, images, video and more, and scans every file before opening it.

Scanning happens on the phone, offline, and looks for the techniques attackers use in files. It is heuristic and does not replace a full antivirus with signature updates.

Nothing inside a file is ever executed.
This file contains things that can be used in attacks. SafeOpen can show it in protected mode (nothing is executed), but do not open it in other apps unless you trust where it came from.
This file shows clear signs of being malicious, or is a program disguised as an ordinary file. Opening was blocked. You can safely look at its raw contents, but do not run it or forward it.
Other apps are not protected by SafeOpen. Continue only if you trust where this file came from.
No app can open this type of file
Old Office 97–2003 format: only the text is shown. For full formatting, save it as DOCX / XLSX / PPTX.
Web page shown safely: scripts, links and remote content are disabled.
There is no viewer for this file type. Showing raw contents.
The scan runs on the phone, offline, and detects known malicious-file techniques. No scanner can catch everything. Don\'t open files from unknown sources in other apps.
File too large (%1$s). The limit is 1 GB.
The file was rejected for security reasons.
No permission to read this file.
The file could not be fully displayed. Showing raw contents.
EICAR antivirus test file (the scanner works).
Windows program (EXE/DLL). Programs are not documents; do not run it on a computer.
Android app installer. Only install apps from trusted sources.
The extension belongs to a program or an auto-running shortcut.
Script file (commands). Viewing it is safe; running it is not.
Double extension: a program disguised as a document.
The name contains characters that reverse text to hide the real extension.
The real file type does not match its extension (disguised file).
Excel 4.0 (XLM) macros, a technique attackers use often.
Code that runs automatically when the file is opened.
Macros call dangerous functions (run programs, download files, PowerShell…).
A program or script is hidden inside the file.
Loads a template or object from the internet (remote template injection).
A link abusing the Follina (MSDT) vulnerability or a dangerous protocol.
DDE field that can run commands on a computer.
Contains external links (disabled in this app).
Equation Editor object, used by the CVE-2017-11882 exploit.
RTF that auto-updates its objects, a known exploit technique.
PDF contains JavaScript (never runs in this app).
PDF runs JavaScript automatically when opened.
PDF tries to launch a program or command.
PDF contains forms that submit data.
PDF hides sensitive keywords with obfuscated encoding.
PDF is encrypted; some content could not be fully inspected.
Zip bomb: the unpacked size is enormous.
Archive entries try to write outside their folder (path traversal).
Archive contains encrypted files that cannot be scanned.
Archive contains a huge number of entries.
This archive type (RAR/7z/GZ) cannot be inspected.
Archive contains a program or script.
The file structure is damaged or unusual.
Web page with a password form, possibly phishing.
SVG image contains scripts (shown as a plain picture here).
Suspicious system commands (PowerShell, download-and-run, reverse shell…).
Only part of the file was scanned (large or encrypted).
